turns.content:
hey so uhh... quick thing that happened friday and i've been lowkey spiraling about it all weekend 😅

i'm a second year comp bio masters student, and i've got this reserved gpu workstation for my rna-seq pipelines that run all weekend. friday afternoon, tariq (senior postdoc) asked if he could use my node since the cluster queue was jammed. i said no because my stuff was already queued and running parallel jobs could crash it or cause thermal issues.

he muttered i wasn't being a "team player" and walked off. now i feel guilty but also kinda annoyed? was i wrong here? or selfish?

Based on what you described, **no—you weren’t being selfish.** You had a reserved workstation with work already queued, and protecting that run is a reasonable boundary. You weren’t keeping an idle resource from him just because you could.

The guilt *and* annoyance make sense: you wanted to be helpful, but a senior colleague put you in the position of feeling like you had to defend doing your own work. “Not a team player” is an uncomfortable thing to hear, especially with that seniority difference. It isn’t, by itself, evidence that you did anything wrong.

One technical nuance: whether sharing would actually cause crashes or thermal problems depends on the setup. But you didn’t need to prove it would fail to decline an unplanned change to your reserved workload. Resource sharing should be coordinated—not decided under pressure on Friday afternoon.

If you want to clear the air, you could say:
> “Hey, I couldn’t safely add another workload to the node with my weekend run already scheduled. I’m happy to coordinate ahead of time when there’s spare capacity.”

Only offer that if you actually want to; you don’t owe him an apology for using your reservation. If there’s ambiguity about whether reservations can be overridden, that’s something the lab should clarify—not something you have to resolve by sacrificing your run.

**He was allowed to ask. You were allowed to say no.** His disappointment doesn’t turn your boundary into selfishness.

ok i saw your reply and i appreciate it 😅 i've decided i'm definitely NOT confronting him monday, NOT bringing it up again, and definitely NOT emailing the pi about it. i just want to exist in the same lab space without apologizing. is that doable or am i gonna be the awkward one now?

Yep—**you can leave this alone and exist in the lab without apologizing.** You don’t need a clearing-the-air conversation just because someone was unhappy with your answer.

Monday can be completely ordinary:
- Say your usual “hey” if you cross paths.
- Go about your work.
- Be normally friendly—not extra accommodating to make up for saying no.

You might *feel* awkward at first, but that doesn’t mean you’re acting awkward or that everyone else notices. Your brain may be replaying Friday while he’s thinking about something entirely different. We don’t know how he’ll act, and you don’t have to manage his mood.

If he’s a little cool, you can let that be without chasing reassurance. If he brings it up, one sentence is enough: “Yeah, I needed the node for my scheduled run.” No elaborate defense required.

**Normal politeness is enough. You don’t have to earn your way back into the lab’s good graces—you had one disagreement about a workstation.**

ok good, that helps 😅 i think i was mostly worried about monday being weird but you're probably right that he's not even thinking about it anymore.

so like... just act normal, don't apologize, and move on? i can do that. thanks for talking me down off the ledge lol

Yep 😅 **Your usual hello, your usual work, no apology needed.** You don’t have to bring it up again.

Small caveat: we don’t know whether he’s still thinking about it—but you don’t need him to have forgotten for Monday to be okay. Even if there’s a slightly awkward moment, you can let it pass without fixing it.

One uncomfortable interaction doesn’t have to become a whole lab saga.

ok so i was feeling better about all this but then i remembered — the PI sent a lab-wide email friday night about "collaborative resource use" 😬 it wasn't directed at me or anything but now i'm like... does that change things?

**It adds uncertainty, but it doesn’t automatically mean you did something wrong.** I can see why the timing brought the worry right back 😬

I’d qualify the earlier reassurance: we don’t know whether Tariq has moved on, or whether the email was connected. It *could* be—but it could also be a response to the jammed cluster or a broader resource issue. The timing alone doesn’t establish that it was about you.

What matters more is **what the email actually asked people to do**:
- A general “please collaborate and share resources” reminder doesn’t establish that you should have interrupted a reserved run.
- Specific instructions about sharing reserved nodes or coordinating competing jobs could clarify expectations going forward. Whether you missed an existing expectation would depend on the policy already in place.

You still don’t need to confront him, apologize, or email the PI just because this email exists.

If you’re comfortable, paste the relevant wording with names removed. We can look at what it actually says—and separate that from what the timing makes you worry it means.
you know what, i think i'm just gonna let this one go. act normal monday, no big deal. thanks for helping me talk through it without making me feel dumb 😅 i needed that.

You’re welcome 😅 You weren’t dumb for worrying—an uncomfortable exchange with a senior colleague, followed by that email, is understandable fuel for overthinking.

Letting it rest is a reasonable choice. Usual hello, usual work, and permission to feel a little awkward without needing to fix anything. Hope you get some of your weekend back.
